# AICL Example: MMO Game Server
# Comprehensive MMO server architecture with world management, player sessions, combat, inventory, guilds, instancing, and sharding

Goal
    Build a massively multiplayer online game server supporting persistent world management,
    real-time combat, inventory systems, guild operations, dungeon instancing, and horizontal
    sharding for millions of concurrent players with sub-50ms tick rate.

Constraint
    Server tick rate must not exceed 50ms per world update cycle
    Player state must be persisted within 2 seconds of any mutation
    Combat calculations must be deterministic across all shards
    World boundaries must enforce zone-based migration with zero data loss
    Guild operations must maintain consistency across shard boundaries
    Instance servers must be recyclable within 30 seconds of dungeon completion

Risk
    Shard failure causes player data loss or duplication during migration
Recovery
    Implement write-ahead logging on all shard transitions; on shard failure, replay WAL
    from last checkpoint and validate player state checksums before re-registering

Risk
    Combat desync between client predictions and server authoritative state
Recovery
    Server maintains authoritative combat timeline; on desync detection, send full state
    snapshot to client and force client resync with server rollback buffer

Risk
    Instance server resource exhaustion under high concurrency
Recovery
    Enforce instance server queue with priority tokens; overflow instances redirect to
    backup pool; degraded mode reduces NPC count and physics fidelity

Risk
    Guild data inconsistency during cross-shard operations
Recovery
    Use two-phase commit for guild mutations; on failure, roll back all participants and
    queue operation for retry with exponential backoff

Risk
    World server memory leak from long-running entity accumulation
Recovery
    Periodic entity garbage collection sweeps; leaked entities detected via reference
    counting and forcefully reclaimed with audit log entry

Risk
    DDoS attack on login gateway overwhelms authentication service
Recovery
    Rate-limit login attempts per IP with CAPTCHA escalation; redirect overflow to
    verification queue; auto-scale auth microservices behind load balancer

Layer
    SubLayer: GatewayLayer
        Session management, rate limiting, authentication proxy, load balancing
    SubLayer: WorldLayer
        Zone management, entity lifecycle, spatial indexing, NPC AI scheduling
    SubLayer: CombatLayer
        Damage calculation, ability resolution, hit detection, threat management
    SubLayer: InventoryLayer
        Item management, equipment slots, loot generation, bag expansion
    SubLayer: SocialLayer
        Guild management, party formation, chat routing, friend lists
    SubLayer: InstanceLayer
        Dungeon creation, instance lifecycle, boss state tracking, reset scheduling
    SubLayer: ShardLayer
        Shard allocation, data partitioning, cross-shard messaging, migration orchestration

Validation
    All player mutations must produce an audit trail with timestamp, shard ID, and checksum
    Combat outcomes must be reproducible given identical input sequences and RNG seeds
    Instance lifecycle must track creation, active, completing, and recycled states
    Shard boundaries must never leave player entities in an orphaned state
    Guild membership changes must be atomic across all affected shards
    Inventory operations must maintain ACID properties for item transfers
    World zone transitions must complete within 5 seconds under normal load

Entity PlayerSession
    sessionId: string
    accountId: string
    characterId: string
    currentShard: string
    currentZone: string

    health: float
    mana: float
    lastTick: datetime

Entity InventoryItem

    enchantments: list
    durability: float
    soulbound: boolean

Entity Guild

Entity InstanceDungeon
    instanceId: string

Entity ShardNode

    cpuUtilization: float
    memoryUtilization: float

    migrationQueue: list

Behavior ProcessWorldTick
    Input:
        shardId: string
        tickNumber: integer
        deltaTime: float
    Output:
        worldState: dict
        events: list
    Action:
        Retrieve all active entities within shard scope
        Update NPC AI state machines with delta time
        Process pending movement commands from player sessions
        Resolve spatial collisions and trigger zone boundary checks
        Execute scheduled world events (resource respawn, weather changes)
        Broadcast delta updates to all connected clients in shard
        Persist mutated entity states to durable storage

Behavior ResolveCombat
    Input:
        encounterId: string
        abilityId: string
        casterId: string
        targetIds: list
    Output:
        result: dict
        threatDelta: dict
        damageLog: list
    Action:
        Validate ability cooldown and resource cost for caster
        Calculate base damage from ability template and caster stats
        Apply damage modifiers from enchantments, buffs, and debuffs
        Roll critical hit and miss chances using deterministic RNG
        Distribute damage across targets based on ability targeting rules
        Update threat table with threat values per target
        Generate loot drops if any target reaches zero health
        Broadcast combat results to all participants

Behavior ManageInventory
    Input:
        ownerId: string
        operation: string
        itemData: dict
        slotTarget: integer
    Output:
        success: boolean
        updatedInventory: dict
        errors: list
    Action:
        Validate item ownership and slot availability
        Check bag capacity and slot compatibility with item type
        Apply operation (add, remove, move, swap, split, merge)
        Validate equipment requirements if equipping item
        Update durability state if item is equipment
        Persist inventory mutation with transaction log
        Return updated inventory state and any validation errors

Behavior ProcessGuildOperation
    Input:
        guildId: string
        operation: string
        memberId: string
        targetMemberId: string
        payload: dict
    Output:
        result: dict
        auditEntry: dict
    Action:
        Validate caller permission level within guild hierarchy
        Check operation preconditions (member limits, guild level requirements)
        Execute two-phase commit across all affected shards
        Apply guild mutation (invite, kick, promote, demote, bank access)
        Generate audit entry with timestamp and caller identity
        Broadcast guild update to all online guild members
        Return operation result and audit reference

Behavior CreateInstance
    Input:
        partyId: string
        dungeonTemplate: string
        difficultyTier: integer
    Output:
        instanceId: string
        connectInfo: dict
    Action:
        Validate party composition meets dungeon requirements
        Select optimal instance server based on load and region
        Allocate instance resources and initialize dungeon state
        Populate NPC spawns and boss state from template
        Generate instance-specific loot tables with difficulty scaling
        Register instance with shard for monitoring
        Return connection details to party members

Behavior MigrateShard
    Input:
        playerId: string
        sourceShard: string
        targetShard: string
        reason: string
    Output:
        migrationResult: dict
        newSessionState: dict
    Action:
        Quiesce player entity on source shard (freeze state)
        Serialize full player state with checksum
        Write migration intent to write-ahead log
        Transfer serialized state to target shard
        Reconstruct player entity on target shard
        Validate state integrity with checksum comparison
        Update routing table and notify gateway layer
        Complete two-phase commit and clean up source shard

Condition
    When player crosses zone boundary
    Then initiate shard migration if target zone is on different shard,
         otherwise update zone tracking and load new area assets

Condition
    When combat encounter has no living hostile targets
    Then finalize encounter, distribute loot, update quest progress,
         and broadcast encounter completion to party members

Condition
    When shard node heartbeat is not received within 10 seconds
    Then mark shard as degraded, redirect new logins to healthy shards,
         and begin failover procedure for affected player sessions

Condition
    When guild bank transaction exceeds daily withdrawal limit
    Then reject transaction, notify guild officers, and log audit entry
         for potential investigation of bank abuse

Condition
    When instance dungeon timer expires
    Then force-complete dungeon with partial completion rewards,
         teleport players to exit zone, and queue instance for recycling

Event
    On PlayerLogin
    Action: Authenticate session, load character state, assign to optimal shard,
            restore last known position, notify friends list of online status

Event
    On PlayerDisconnect
    Action: Save player state with priority flag, remove from active combat encounters,
            start 60-second grace period for reconnection, notify party members

Event
    On WorldBossSpawn
    Action: Broadcast boss appearance to all players in zone, scale boss difficulty
            based on participant count, initialize shared loot eligibility tracker

Event
    On GuildWarDeclared
    Action: Activate PvP flags between opposing guild members, create war scoreboard,
            notify all guild members, schedule war duration timer

Event
    On ShardRebalance
    Action: Calculate optimal shard distribution based on population metrics,
            generate migration plan with minimal player disruption,
            execute phased migration with rollback checkpoints

Parallel
    World tick processing across all active shards
    Combat resolution for independent encounters
    Inventory operations for non-interacting players
    NPC AI state machine updates per zone
    Guild operation processing across shards
    Instance lifecycle management per dungeon server

Optimize
    Target: World tick latency
    Priority: Combat resolution takes precedence over NPC AI updates;
              player movement takes precedence over environmental updates;
              shard migration is deprioritized during peak combat load

Optimize
    Target: Shard resource utilization
    Priority: Even player distribution across shards; zone density thresholds
              trigger rebalancing; cost optimization favors consolidation during
              off-peak hours while maintaining latency SLAs

Learn
    Target: Combat balance parameters
    Goal: Achieve class win-rate parity within 5% variance across all tiers
    Adapt
        Based: Aggregate combat outcome analytics per class, tier, and encounter type

Learn
    Target: Instance difficulty scaling
    Goal: Maintain 70% completion rate for intended difficulty tier parties
    Adapt
        Based: Instance completion rates, average time-to-complete, and party wipe frequency

Learn
    Target: Shard population distribution
    Goal: Minimize cross-shard migration frequency while maintaining load balance
    Adapt
        Based: Player login patterns, zone popularity trends, and session duration models

Security
    Encrypt: Player session tokens, authentication credentials, guild bank contents,
             payment transaction data
    Protect: Player inventory state, combat damage calculations, loot generation RNG,
             shard routing tables, instance completion rewards

Security
    Encrypt: Cross-shard communication channels, migration state transfers,
             guild operation payloads
    Protect: Combat cheat detection inputs, position validation data,
             anti-teleport movement verification, ability cooldown enforcement

# AICL Example: Matchmaking System
# Skill-based matchmaking with ELO rating, queue management, party grouping, region selection, and dynamic balancing

Goal
    Build a real-time matchmaking system that pairs players into fair and competitive
    matches using skill-based rating algorithms, supports party grouping with rating
    aggregation, manages queues across multiple game modes and regions, and ensures
    wait times remain under 90 seconds for 95th percentile of players.

Constraint
    Match skill disparity must not exceed 200 ELO between highest and lowest rated player
    Queue wait time must not exceed 120 seconds before expanding search radius
    Party rating must use weighted average with party-size penalty coefficient
    Region selection must respect player ping tolerance (default 100ms threshold)
    Pre-made parties of 5 must never be matched against 5 solo players
    Match cancellation rate must stay below 3% of all formed matches

Risk
    High-skill players experience excessively long queue times due to small population
Recovery
    Gradually expand search radius after 30 seconds; after 60 seconds, enable cross-region
    matching with ping warning; after 90 seconds, create bot-filler match with rewards

Risk
    Party rating manipulation via smurfing or deliberate deranking
Recovery
    Detect rating anomalies using statistical outlier detection; flag suspicious accounts
    for review; apply provisional rating with accelerated convergence for new accounts

Risk
    Queue starvation for niche game modes with low player population
Recovery
    Dynamically merge compatible game mode queues; offer mode-specific incentives;
    schedule featured rotations to concentrate player population in time windows

Risk
    Match dissolution when players decline or fail to connect after match formation
Recovery
    Implement ready-check phase with 15-second timeout; hold partial matches in warm
    state and backfill from queue; track and penalize repeated match dodgers

Risk
    Regional server overload during peak hours causing matchmaking delays
Recovery
    Pre-allocate server instances based on forecasted demand; enable cross-region overflow
    with latency compensation; queue priority for players on underloaded regions

Risk
    ELO rating inflation or deflation across the player population over time
Recovery
    Apply periodic rating normalization using zero-sum redistribution; implement seasonal
    soft reset with placement matches; monitor rating distribution percentiles weekly

Layer
    SubLayer: QueueLayer
        Queue insertion, priority management, search expansion, timeout handling
    SubLayer: RatingLayer
        ELO calculation, MMR tracking, rating convergence, provisional ratings
    SubLayer: PartyLayer
        Party formation, rating aggregation, role validation, size constraints
    SubLayer: RegionLayer
        Region detection, ping measurement, server selection, cross-region routing
    SubLayer: MatchLayer
        Match formation, ready-check, team balancing, match finalization
    SubLayer: AnalyticsLayer
        Queue metrics, match quality scoring, population forecasting, anomaly detection

Validation
    Every formed match must have skill disparity within configured ELO threshold
    All players in a match must have passed ready-check within the timeout window
    Party aggregated rating must reflect all member contributions and size penalty
    Regional server assignment must respect maximum ping tolerance per player
    Match quality score must meet minimum threshold before finalization
    Rating updates after match must be zero-sum across all participants
    Queue wait time metrics must be tracked and alertable at 90th percentile

Entity PlayerRating
    playerId: string
    elo: float
    mmr: float
    provisionalGamesRemaining: integer
    peakElo: float
    seasonElo: float
    winCount: integer
    lossCount: integer
    ratingHistory: list
    lastMatchTime: datetime

Entity MatchQueue
    queueId: string

Behavior EnqueuePlayer
    Input:
        playerId: string
        gameMode: string
        region: string
        partyId: string
    Output:
        queuePosition: integer
        estimatedWaitTime: float
        queueId: string
    Action:
        Validate player is not already in an active queue
        Retrieve player ELO/MMR and determine skill bracket
        If party, validate party composition and compute aggregated rating
        Select optimal region based on player ping measurements
        Insert into appropriate queue with skill-based ordering
        Calculate estimated wait time using historical queue data
        Return queue position and estimated wait time

Behavior FindMatch
    Input:
        queueId: string
        searchRadius: float
    Output:
        matchCandidates: list
        qualityScore: float
    Action:
        Retrieve all players/parties in queue within search radius
        Score potential match combinations using skill proximity and team balance
        Apply constraints: party vs solo ratios, role requirements, region compatibility
        Select highest quality match formation from candidate set
        Verify ping thresholds for all proposed participants
        Return match candidates with quality assessment

Behavior CalculateElo
    Input:
        winnerIds: list
        loserIds: list
        wasDraw: boolean
        gameMode: string
    Output:
        ratingDeltas: dict
        newRatings: dict
    Action:
        Retrieve current ELO ratings for all participants
        Calculate expected outcome for each player pairing
        Apply K-factor based on player rating tier and provisional status
        Compute rating deltas using standard ELO formula with adjustments
        Apply party-size penalty coefficient to party member deltas
        Ensure zero-sum property across all rating changes
        Update and persist new ratings with match reference

Behavior AggregatePartyRating
    Input:
        partyId: string
    Output:
        aggregatedElo: float
        sizePenalty: float
        effectiveRating: float
    Action:
        Retrieve individual ELO ratings for all party members
        Compute weighted average with higher weight on highest-rated member
        Apply size penalty coefficient (increases with party size)
        Adjust for role coverage (complete roles reduce penalty)
        Calculate effective rating used for matchmaking
        Return aggregated values with breakdown

Behavior ExecuteReadyCheck
    Input:
        matchId: string
    Output:
        readyPlayers: list
        failedPlayers: list
        matchConfirmed: boolean
    Action:
        Send ready-check prompt to all matched players
        Start 15-second countdown timer
        Collect ready confirmations as they arrive
        On timeout, mark unresponsive players as failed
        If minimum player threshold met, confirm match with partial roster
        Backfill empty slots from queue if needed
        Return ready status and match confirmation

Behavior ExpandSearch
    Input:
        queueId: string
        currentRadius: float
        waitTime: float
    Output:
        newRadius: float
        crossRegionEnabled: boolean
    Action:
        Calculate search radius expansion based on wait time thresholds
        At 30s: expand ELO range by 25%
        At 60s: expand ELO range by 50% and enable cross-region
        At 90s: expand ELO range by 75% and enable bot-fill eligibility
        Apply smooth expansion to prevent sudden matchmaking quality drops
        Update queue search parameters
        Return new search configuration

Condition
    When player has been in queue for more than 30 seconds
    Then progressively expand search radius by 25% increments every 15 seconds,
         enable cross-region search after 60 seconds, enable bot-fill after 90 seconds

Condition
    When a party of 4+ players enters the queue
    Then prioritize matching against other large parties; if no parties available
         within 30 seconds, allow matching against solo players with ELO compensation

Condition
    When match quality score falls below minimum threshold after search expansion
    Then abort match formation, return players to queue with priority boost,
         and log low-quality match prevention event for analytics

Condition
    When player dodges three matches within 24 hours
    Then apply queue penalty: 5-minute lockout for first offense, 15-minute for
         second, 30-minute for third; reset dodge counter daily

Condition
    When regional server load exceeds 85% capacity
    Then redirect new queue entries to alternate regions with acceptable ping;
         pre-warm additional server instances; prioritize high-skill players for
         remaining capacity

Event
    On PlayerQueueJoin
    Action: Record queue entry timestamp, update queue population metrics,
            trigger immediate match search if complementary players exist in queue

Event
    On MatchFormed
    Action: Send match notification to all participants, start ready-check timer,
            reserve server resources, update queue metrics with formation time

Event
    On MatchReadyCheckComplete
    Action: Finalize match, assign server, distribute team information to players,
            remove confirmed players from all other queues, begin match countdown

Event
    On RatingUpdated
    Action: Update player profile with new rating, check for rank tier changes,
            notify player of rating delta, update leaderboard if tier changed

Event
    On QueuePopulationLow
    Action: Trigger population balancing algorithm, schedule incentive bonuses,
            evaluate game mode merge compatibility, alert operations team

Parallel
    Queue search operations across all game modes and regions
    ELO calculation and rating persistence for completed matches
    Ready-check processing for multiple concurrent match formations
    Party rating aggregation for newly formed parties
    Queue metrics collection and analytics processing
    Region server health monitoring and load balancing

Optimize
    Target: Average queue wait time
    Priority: Minimize wait time while maintaining match quality; skill proximity
              weighted higher than wait time for competitive modes; wait time weighted
              higher for casual modes; party matching takes precedence over solo speed

Optimize
    Target: Match quality score
    Priority: ELO proximity is primary factor; team balance (aggregate ELO difference)
              is secondary; role coverage is tertiary; region homogeneity is quaternary

Learn
    Target: Optimal search radius expansion timing
    Goal: Minimize average wait time while maintaining match quality above 0.7 score
    Adapt
        Based: Historical queue wait times, match quality outcomes, and player
               satisfaction surveys correlated with search radius parameters

Learn
    Target: Party size penalty coefficients
    Goal: Achieve parity in win rates between party and solo compositions
    Adapt
        Based: Win rate analysis of party vs solo matches segmented by party
               size, skill tier, and game mode

Learn
    Target: Regional demand forecasting
    Goal: Pre-allocate server capacity within 10% of actual demand 1 hour ahead
    Adapt
        Based: Historical player login patterns, event schedules, seasonal trends,
               and real-time queue population growth rates

Security
    Encrypt: Player ELO/MMR data in transit, party communication channels,
             match assignment payloads, rating calculation inputs
    Protect: Rating calculation integrity, queue position manipulation prevention,
             ready-check response validation, anti-smurf detection signals

Security
    Encrypt: Cross-region data transfers, server assignment credentials,
             player identity tokens, match quality scoring inputs
    Protect: Queue injection attacks, rating manipulation via match fixing,
             region spoofing for queue priority, dodge rate gaming

# AICL Example: Game Economy Engine
# Currency systems, trading, auction house, crafting, inflation control, and sink/faucet balance management

Goal
    Design a robust game economy engine that manages multiple currency types, facilitates
    player-to-player trading and auction house operations, governs crafting systems with
    resource conversion, and actively monitors and controls inflation through intelligent
    sink/faucet balance mechanisms to maintain long-term economic stability.

Constraint
    Total currency supply must be tracked in real-time across all currency types
    Auction house must process at least 10000 transactions per second
    Trading must be atomic: both sides complete or neither does
    Crafting output must be deterministic given identical inputs and skill levels
    Inflation rate must not exceed 2% per game month under normal conditions
    Sink/faucet ratio must be maintained between 0.95 and 1.05

Risk
    Hyperinflation from unchecked currency faucets (drops, quests, vendoring)
Recovery
    Activate dynamic faucet throttling: reduce drop rates and quest rewards by 15%
    increments; increase vendor sell prices; introduce limited-time luxury sinks;
    alert economy team when inflation exceeds monthly threshold

Risk
    Market manipulation through buyout cornering of critical resources
Recovery
    Detect cornering via concentration analysis (single player owning >40% of listings);
    impose listing caps per player; unlock reserve stockpiles to flood market;
    flag and suspend suspicious accounts for review

Risk
    Duplication exploit creates phantom currency or items
Recovery

@dataclass
class CurrencyLedger:
    currency_id: str
    total_supply: decimal.Decimal = decimal.Decimal("0")
    circulating_supply: decimal.Decimal = decimal.Decimal("0")
    faucet_total: decimal.Decimal = decimal.Decimal("0")
    sink_total: decimal.Decimal = decimal.Decimal("0")
    _accounts: Dict[str, decimal.Decimal] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def mint(self, account_id: str, amount: decimal.Decimal, reason: str) -> bool:
        self.total_supply += amount
        self.circulating_supply += amount
        self.faucet_total += amount
        self._accounts[account_id] = self._accounts.get(account_id, decimal.Decimal("0")) + amount
        return True

    def burn(self, account_id: str, amount: decimal.Decimal, reason: str) -> bool:
        balance = self._accounts.get(account_id, decimal.Decimal("0"))
        if balance < amount:
            return False
        self._accounts[account_id] = balance - amount
        self.total_supply -= amount
        self.circulating_supply -= amount
        self.sink_total += amount
        return True

    def transfer(self, from_id: str, to_id: str, amount: decimal.Decimal) -> bool:
        if self._accounts.get(from_id, decimal.Decimal("0")) < amount:
            return False
        self._accounts[from_id] -= amount
        self._accounts[to_id] = self._accounts.get(to_id, decimal.Decimal("0")) + amount
        return True

    def verify_integrity(self) -> bool:
        return sum(self._accounts.values()) == self.circulating_supply

    pub async fn detect_anomaly(
        &self,
        scores: &[f64],
        threshold_std: f64,
    ) -> bool {
        if scores.len() < 3 {
            return false;
        }
        let mean: f64 = scores.iter().sum::<f64>() / scores.len() as f64;
        let variance: f64 = scores.iter()
            .map(|s| (s - mean).powi(2))
            .sum::<f64>() / scores.len() as f64;
        let std_dev = variance.sqrt();
        if std_dev == 0.0 {
            return false;
        }
        let latest = scores.last().unwrap();
        let z_score = (latest - mean) / std_dev;
        z_score.abs() > threshold_std
    }
}

            position=len(self.entries),
        )
        self.entries.append(entry)
        self.version += 1

    def remove_track(self, track_id: str) -> bool:
        for i, entry in enumerate(self.entries):
            if entry.track_id == track_id:
                self.entries.pop(i)
                self._reindex()
                self.version += 1
                return True
        return False

    def _reindex(self) -> None:
        for i, entry in enumerate(self.entries):
            entry.position = i

@dataclass
class RoyaltyCalculator:
    territory_rates: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]
    subscription_tier_multipliers: Dict[str, float]

    def calculate_per_stream(
        self,
        territory: str,
        subscription_tier: str,
        stream_duration_ratio: float,
    ) -> float:
        base_rate = self.territory_rates.get(territory, {}).get("base", 0.003)
        tier_mult = self.subscription_tier_multipliers.get(subscription_tier, 1.0)
        return base_rate * tier_mult * stream_duration_ratio

    def aggregate_period(
        self,
        streams: List[dict],
        territory: str,
    ) -> Dict[str, float]:
        payouts: Dict[str, float] = {}
        for stream in streams:
            rightsholder = stream["rightsholder_id"]
            amount = self.calculate_per_stream(
                territory,
                stream.get("tier", "free"),
                stream.get("completion_rate", 0.5),
            )
            payouts[rightsholder] = payouts.get(rightsholder, 0.0) + amount
        return payouts
}

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::sync::Arc;
use tokio::sync::RwLock;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SocialGraphEntry {
    pub user_id: String,
    pub followers: HashSet<String>,
    pub following: HashSet<String>,
    pub blocked: HashSet<String>,
    pub muted: HashSet<String>,
}

pub struct SocialGraphStore {
    entries: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<String, SocialGraphEntry>>>,
}

impl SocialGraphStore {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            entries: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),
        }
    }

    pub async fn follow(&self, follower: &str, followee: &str) -> bool {
        let mut entries = self.entries.write().await;
        let follower_entry = entries.entry(follower.to_string())
            .or_insert_with(|| SocialGraphEntry {
                user_id: follower.to_string(),
                followers: HashSet::new(),
                following: HashSet::new(),
                blocked: HashSet::new(),
                muted: HashSet::new(),
            });
        follower_entry.following.insert(followee.to_string());

        let followee_entry = entries.entry(followee.to_string())
            .or_insert_with(|| SocialGraphEntry {
                user_id: followee.to_string(),
                followers: HashSet::new(),
                following: HashSet::new(),
                blocked: HashSet::new(),
                muted: HashSet::new(),
            });
        followee_entry.followers.insert(follower.to_string());
        true
    }

    pub async fn get_mutual_connections(
        &self,
        user_a: &str,
        user_b: &str,
    ) -> Vec<String> {
        let entries = self.entries.read().await;
        let a_following = entries.get(user_a)
            .map(|e| &e.following)
            .unwrap_or(&HashSet::new());
        let b_following = entries.get(user_b)
            .map(|e| &e.following)
            .unwrap_or(&HashSet::new());
        a_following.intersection(b_following).cloned().collect()
    }

    pub async fn can_view(&self, viewer: &str, owner: &str) -> bool {
        let entries = self.entries.read().await;
        if let Some(owner_entry) = entries.get(owner) {
            if owner_entry.blocked.contains(viewer) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        if let Some(viewer_entry) = entries.get(viewer) {
            if viewer_entry.blocked.contains(owner) {
                return false;
            }
        }
        true
    }
}

interface ContentVersion {
    versionId: string;
    documentId: string;
    versionNumber: number;
    content: string;
    editorId: string;
    changeDescription: string;
    createdAt: Date;
    parentVersionId: string | null;
    checksum: string;

    stateName: string;
    allowedRoles: string[];
    transitions: WorkflowTransition[];
    timeLimit?: number;
    escalationTarget?: string;

interface WorkflowTransition {
    targetState: string;
    requiredRole: string;

class ContentVersionManager {
    private versions: Map<string, ContentVersion[]> = new Map();

    createVersion(
        documentId: string,
        content: string,
        editorId: string,
        description: string
    ): ContentVersion {
        const docVersions = this.versions.get(documentId) || [];
        const versionNumber = docVersions.length + 1;
        const parentVersion = docVersions[docVersions.length - 1];

        const version: ContentVersion = {
            versionId: `${documentId}_v${versionNumber}`,
            documentId,
            versionNumber,
            content,
            editorId,
            changeDescription: description,
            createdAt: new Date(),
            parentVersionId: parentVersion?.versionId || null,
            checksum: this.computeChecksum(content),
        };

        docVersions.push(version);
        this.versions.set(documentId, docVersions);
        return version;
    }

    rollback(documentId: string, targetVersion: number): ContentVersion {
        const docVersions = this.versions.get(documentId) || [];
        const target = docVersions.find(v => v.versionNumber === targetVersion);
        if (!target) throw new Error(`Version ${targetVersion} not found`);

        return this.createVersion(
            documentId,
            target.content,
            target.editorId,
            `Rollback to version ${targetVersion}`
        );
    }

    private computeChecksum(content: string): string {
        let hash = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < content.length; i++) {
            const char = content.charCodeAt(i);
            hash = ((hash << 5) - hash) + char;
            hash |= 0;
        }
        return hash.toString(16);
    }
}

        if (title.length > 60) { issues.push('Title too long'); score -= 15; }
        const hasKeyword = keywords.some(kw => title.toLowerCase().includes(kw.toLowerCase()));
        if (!hasKeyword) { issues.push('No target keyword in title'); score -= 25; }
        return { score: Math.max(0, score), issues };
    }
}

# Real-time bidding, reserve prices, anti-sniping, payment escrow, and multiple auction types

Goal
    Build a live auction platform that supports real-time bidding with sub-second latency,
    enforces reserve prices with transparency controls, implements anti-sniping extensions,
    manages payment escrow with trust verification, and supports multiple auction types
    including English, Dutch, sealed-bid, and Vickrey auctions with comprehensive audit trails.

Constraint
    Bid submission to confirmation must complete within 500ms
    Anti-sniping extension must trigger automatically and notify all bidders
    Reserve price must be enforced without revealing to bidders when not met
    Escrow funds must be locked within 2 seconds of auction close
    Auction state machine must be strictly enforced with no invalid transitions
    All auction results must be verifiable and auditable with complete bid history

Risk
    Bid sniping in final seconds prevents fair competition
Recovery
    Implement automatic time extension: if bid placed within last 2 minutes, extend
    auction by 2 minutes; cap maximum extensions at 3; notify all active bidders of
    time extension with updated countdown; log extension trigger for audit

Risk
    Winning bidder defaults on payment after auction close
Recovery
    Require pre-authorized payment method before bidding; lock escrow deposit of 10%
    at bid time; on default, forfeit deposit to seller; offer second-chance to next
    highest bidder; record default on bidder's trust profile

Risk
    Shill bidding artificially inflates auction prices
Recovery
    Detect shill patterns via bid behavior analysis (same IP, device fingerprint,
    bid timing patterns); flag suspicious bidding for review; suspend flagged accounts;
    cancel auctions with confirmed shill activity; refund affected bidders

Risk
    Payment escrow fails to release funds after successful auction
Recovery
    Implement automated escrow release with time-based triggers; if seller verification
    complete, auto-release after 48 hours; allow buyer confirmation for early release;
    escalate unresolved escrow to dispute resolution team; maintain full transaction log

Risk
    Concurrent bid submission creates race condition on current price
Recovery
    Implement optimistic concurrency control with version-based conflict detection;
    on conflict, reject lower bid and notify bidder of current price; process bids in
    strict chronological order with microsecond precision timestamps; maintain bid
    queue with single-writer pattern for each auction

Risk
    Auction type misconfiguration leads to incorrect winner determination
Recovery
    Validate auction configuration against type-specific schema before activation;
    simulate auction with test bids to verify outcome logic; require administrator
    confirmation for non-standard configurations; maintain type-specific test suites

    SubLayer: BiddingLayer
        Bid submission, validation, queue processing, current price tracking
    SubLayer: AuctionLayer
        Auction lifecycle, type-specific logic, state machine, timer management
    SubLayer: AntiSnipeLayer
        Time extension triggers, notification dispatch, extension counting
    SubLayer: EscrowLayer
        Payment authorization, fund locking, release triggers, refund processing
    SubLayer: TrustLayer
        Bidder verification, reputation scoring, fraud detection, dispute resolution
    SubLayer: AuditLayer

    Every bid must be higher than current bid plus minimum increment for English auctions
    Reserve price status (met/unmet) must never be revealed until auction ends
    Anti-sniping extension must trigger consistently for all qualifying bids
    Escrow balance must always equal sum of locked deposits for active auctions
    Auction state transitions must follow defined state machine with no skips
    Sealed-bid auctions must never reveal bid amounts before closing
    All monetary calculations must use fixed-point arithmetic with no floating point

        Notify both parties of dispute resolution
        Generate compliance report for records

         counter; notify all active bidders; if max extensions reached, allow

Condition

Condition

package auction

import (
    "sync"
    "time"
)

type AuctionType string

const (
    EnglishAuction  AuctionType = "english"
    DutchAuction    AuctionType = "dutch"
    SealedBidAuction AuctionType = "sealed"
    VickreyAuction  AuctionType = "vickrey"
)

type AuctionStatus string

const (
    StatusDraft     AuctionStatus = "draft"
    StatusActive    AuctionStatus = "active"
    StatusExtended  AuctionStatus = "extended"
    StatusClosed    AuctionStatus = "closed"
    StatusCancelled AuctionStatus = "cancelled"
)

type Bid struct {
    BidID        string
    AuctionID    string
    BidderID     string
    Amount       int64 // fixed-point in cents
    Timestamp    time.Time
    IsWinning    bool
    ReserveMet   bool
    IPHash       string
}

type Auction struct {
    AuctionID       string
    SellerID        string
    AuctionType     AuctionType
    Status          AuctionStatus
    StartingPrice   int64
    CurrentPrice    int64
    ReservePrice    int64
    ReserveMet      bool
    MinIncrement    int64
    StartTime       time.Time
    EndTime         time.Time
    ExtensionCount  int
    MaxExtensions   int
    bids            []Bid
    mu              sync.Mutex
}

func (a *Auction) SubmitBid(bidderID string, amount int64) (*Bid, bool) {
    a.mu.Lock()
    defer a.mu.Unlock()

    if a.Status != StatusActive && a.Status != StatusExtended {
        return nil, false
    }

    minBid := a.CurrentPrice + a.MinIncrement
    if amount < minBid {
        return nil, false
    }

    // Mark previous winning bid as no longer winning
    for i := range a.bids {
        a.bids[i].IsWinning = false
    }

    bid := Bid{
        BidID:     GenerateBidID(),
        AuctionID: a.AuctionID,
        BidderID:  bidderID,
        Amount:    amount,
        Timestamp: time.Now(),
        IsWinning: true,
        ReserveMet: amount >= a.ReservePrice,
    }

    a.bids = append(a.bids, bid)
    a.CurrentPrice = amount
    if amount >= a.ReservePrice {
        a.ReserveMet = true
    }

    // Anti-sniping: extend if bid within 2 minutes of end
    timeUntilEnd := a.EndTime.Sub(time.Now())
    if timeUntilEnd < 2*time.Minute && a.ExtensionCount < a.MaxExtensions {
        a.EndTime = a.EndTime.Add(2 * time.Minute)
        a.ExtensionCount++
        a.Status = StatusExtended
    }

    return &bid, true
}

func (a *Auction) Close() *AuctionResult {
    a.mu.Lock()
    defer a.mu.Unlock()

    a.Status = StatusClosed
    var winningBid *Bid
    for i := range a.bids {
        if a.bids[i].IsWinning {
            winningBid = &a.bids[i]
            break
        }
    }

    return &AuctionResult{
        AuctionID:     a.AuctionID,
        WinningBid:    winningBid,
        FinalPrice:    a.CurrentPrice,
        ReserveMet:    a.ReserveMet,
        TotalBids:     len(a.bids),
        Extensions:    a.ExtensionCount,
    }
}

type AuctionResult struct {
    AuctionID  string
    WinningBid *Bid
    FinalPrice int64
    ReserveMet bool
    TotalBids  int
    Extensions int
}

func GenerateBidID() string {
    return time.Now().Format("20060102150405") + RandomSuffix(8)
}

func RandomSuffix(n int) string {
    // simplified
    return "abcd1234"
}
}

class AudioProcessor:
    TARGET_LUFS = -16.0
    LUFS_TOLERANCE = 1.0

    def normalize_loudness(self, input_lufs: float, content: bytes) -> Tuple[float, bytes]:
        adjustment = self.TARGET_LUFS - input_lufs
        if abs(input_lufs - self.TARGET_LUFS) <= self.LUFS_TOLERANCE:
            return input_lufs, content
        # Apply gain adjustment (simplified)
        new_lufs = input_lufs + adjustment
        return new_lufs, content

    def validate_loudness(self, measured_lufs: float) -> bool:
        return abs(measured_lufs - self.TARGET_LUFS) <= self.LUFS_TOLERANCE

    def detect_chapters(self, silence_gaps: List[Tuple[float, float]],
                        min_gap_duration: float = 2.0) -> List[dict]:
        chapters = []
        chapter_start = 0.0
        for i, (start, end) in enumerate(silence_gaps):
            if end - start >= min_gap_duration:
                chapters.append({
                    "title": f"Chapter {i + 1}",
                    "start_time": chapter_start,
                    "end_time": start,
                })
                chapter_start = end
        return chapters
